Definition: Beth-ha-Ram, a place East of the Jordan
BiblicalUsage: Beth-Haran means house of the joyful shouter, and it appears once, in Numbers 32:36, where the Gadites built Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran as fenced cities, with folds for sheep. A fortified town with a glad name, built by men settling down east of the Jordan.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a fenced city with a joyful name is a good picture of settling into what God has given.
